stories.headline: J-K LG condemns Kulgam terror attack, says security forces given free hand to hunt down terrorists
stories.title: J-K LG condemns Kulgam terror attack, says security forces given free hand to hunt down terrorists
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 11: Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha on Wednesday reviewed security situation following Kulgam terror attack and said security forces have been given a free hand to crack down on terrorists in Jammu and Kashmir. The LG Sinha visited Army’s 92 Base Hospital in Srinagar and enquired about the health of CRPF head constable Sonbir Singh who sustained serious injuries in the attack. In a post on X, Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha said: “Visited Base Hospital, Srinagar, to enquire about the health of CRPF Head Constable Sonbir Singh, who sustained serious injuries in the heinous terror attack in Kulgam and is currently undergoing treatment. Praying for his swift and complete recovery. Two other injured CRPF personnel, Constable Rakesh Das and Constable Santanu Chandra, are in stable condition and recovering at 46 Bn CRPF Unit Hospital, Kulgam. I strongly condemn this cowardly act of terror and assure the people that those responsible will be hunted down and brought to justice,” he said. The Lieutenant Governor also reviewed the security situation with senior official in Lok Bhavan, Srinagar and said that security forces have been given a free hand to crack down on terrorists.

stories.headline: Cyclone over Bay may bring rains to Telangana
stories.title: Cyclone over Bay may bring rains to Telangana
stories.summary: Bay low-pressure system likely to intensify
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Hyderabad: Telangana is expected to witness rains after November 21 due to a low pressure and depression forming in the Bay of Bengal under the influence of Cyclone Akvan.
According to weather expert T Balaji, a low pressure system will form on Friday, intensifying into a depression on Sunday, with a 100 per cent probability of developing into a cyclone by Tuesday.
The cyclone is likely to cross between Nellore or Ongole and Odisha or Bengal around November 19 to 20.

Outlining possible scenarios, Balaji noted a 55 per cent chance of the system moving towards Andhra Pradesh, triggering moderate to heavy rains in East Telangana between November 21 and 24 while other regions remain dry.
A 25 per cent probability towards Odisha or Bengal would keep Telangana dry while easing cold conditions after November 20.
A 20 per cent chance towards Bangladesh or Myanmar would cause a severe cold wave with plunging temperatures and dry weather.

Meanwhile, the India Meteorological Department forecasted dry weather across Telangana, noting minimum temperatures will remain 2 to 3°C below normal for the next two to three days, continuing until November 18.

stories.headline: Cyclone Murasu damages over 274 hectares of crop area in Prakasam district
stories.title: Cyclone Murasu damages over 274 hectares of crop area in Prakasam district
stories.summary: District Agriculture Officer says maize suffered the maximum damage across 154.17 hectares, followed by paddy and cotton crops sown on 66.02 hectares and 49.78 hectares respectively; APCPDCL restores power across 613 cyclone-affected villages in the district
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: More than 274 hectares of agricultural crop area was damaged across seven mandals in Prakasam district due to Cyclone Murasu, affecting the livelihoods of 371 farmers, District Agriculture Officer (DAO) Srinivasa Rao told.
The Hindu.
The seven mandals include Ballikurava, J. Pangulur, Mundlamuru, Addanki, Santhamaguluru, Naguluppalapadu and Korisapadu.
Of the total enumerated area of 274.19 hectares, the Agriculture Department has approved 267.08 hectares and rejected 7.11 hectares.

According to information provided by the District Agriculture Officer, maize is the major crop in the district and has suffered the maximum damage across 154.17 hectares, followed by paddy and cotton crops sown on 66.02 hectares and 49.78 hectares respectively.
Black gram and sugarcane are the other crops that have also suffered damage due the heavy rains triggered by the cyclone.
The paddy fields in Kothareddypalem, Singarakondapalem, Dharmavaram, Kalavakuru and Chinakothapalli villages in Addanki mandal were inundated.
Meanwhile, the power infrastructure in the region suffered severe damage following heavy rains and strong winds triggered by the cyclone.
Owing to the disrupted power supply and lack of irrigation, the borewell-irrigated fields have turned dry, with cracks appearing in the soil.
The Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Company Limited (APCPDCL) has almost completed the power restoration works across 613 Cyclone Murasu-affected villages in Prakasam district.
Nearly 90 per cent of the repair works in agriculture and aquaculture connections has also been completed.

Speaking to The Hindu, APCPDCL Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) Pogaku Pulla Reddy said, “Of the 28,907 cyclone-affected connections, 22,887 have been rectified and only 6,020 are pending in agriculture segment, while 125 services are yet to be rectified in the non agriculture segment.”

stories.headline: Ladakh Police remove Sonam Wangchuk from protest site amid election curbs
stories.title: Ladakh Police remove Sonam Wangchuk from protest site amid election curbs
stories.summary: Ladakh Police remove Sonam Wangchuk from protest site amid election curbs
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Ladakh Police removed Sonam Wangchuk from his Leh protest site under election-related prohibitory orders.
His subsequent appeal spotlighted concerns over the inquiry, democratic safeguards and winter polling.

Ladakh Police on Wednesday removed climate activist Sonam Wangchuk from his protest site in Leh and escorted him to his residence, advising him to remain at home in view of prohibitory orders restricting public gatherings during the ongoing election process.
In a statement, the police said the preventive action was taken in compliance with orders issued by the Chief Electoral Officer of the Union Territory of Ladakh and the District Magistrate, Leh.
The orders prohibit public rallies, protests and other gatherings within the limits of Leh Municipality.

"Shri Sonam Wangchuk has been advised to stay at his residence," the police said, adding that the action was taken under the prevailing prohibitory orders to prevent any potential breach of public order and maintain peace and tranquillity.

The police also urged people to comply with the restrictions in view of the Panchayat, Municipal and Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council (LAHDC) elections and refrain from activities that could disrupt public order.

Following the police action, Wangchuk posted a video message on X, appealing to President Droupadi Murmu, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and the people of India to intervene in the situation in Ladakh.

In his message, titled "Ladakh's SOS Appeal to the Nation", Wangchuk alleged that the judicial inquiry into the September 24 incidents in Leh was progressing slowly, more than a year after the events.
He also claimed that talks on restoring democracy in the Union Territory had broken down.

Questioning the timing and conduct of the upcoming council elections, Wangchuk alleged that the administration was pushing ahead with the polls to install people of its choice to negotiate on issues concerning democracy and safeguards for Ladakh.

He also raised concerns over the proposed election schedule, pointing out that December and January are the coldest and snowiest months in the region, with temperatures falling below minus 30 degrees Celsius in several places.

stories.headline: Navi Mumbai Airport shift: CM offers a different flight plan
stories.title: Navi Mumbai Airport shift: CM offers a different flight plan
stories.summary: As airlines begin shifting flights from Mumbai’s Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (CSMIA) to the Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMIA), Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has objected to Mumbai International Airport Ltd’s (MIAL) plan to move 14 international flights to NMIA from the summer 2027 schedule.According to a report by The Times of India on November 10, Fadnavis has proposed an alternative sequence for the redevelopment of Terminal 1, beginning with the development of Terminal 1B before shifting operations from 1A and demolishing the existing terminal. “I have written to them to first develop Terminal 1B, shift 1A to 1B and then take down the existing 1A terminal,” he told the newspaper.The debate over the proposed shift has been simmering for some time, with passengers raising concerns about the additional cost and time involved in travelling to the new airport, as well as the logistical challenges of making connecting flights. Airlines, too, are unhappy with loss of slots and operational complications.Also Read: IndiGo, Air India Express to Shift International Flights to Navi MumbaiWhy flights are movingPlans to reconstruct Terminal 1B date back to 2018, when MIAL, then controlled by the GVK Group, proposed a phased redevelopment estimated to cost around Rs1,200 crore, to address issues, including corrosion and cracks identified in an audit. However, the plan was deferred during the Covid-19 pandemic and delayed further by the lack of an alternative facility to accommodate airlines during construction.In January 2025, MIAL, now under Adani Airport Holdings, announced that work would begin in November, with Terminal 2 and NMIA expected to absorb the displaced traffic. The plan was deferred because NMIA was not ready to accommodate the affected airlines. Now the airport operator plans to begin work on the north section of Terminal 1B in January 2027. The project is expected to raise the terminal’s annual capacity from 15 million passengers to 20 million by 2030. Currently, Mumbai Airport handles around 55 million passengers annually.MIAL told the Airports Economic Regulatory Authority (AERA) that the ageing terminal had become structurally weak and needed reconstruction to improve safety, passenger facilities and operational efficiency.Also Read: Mumbai Airport to Cut 265 Weekly International Flights Amid Terminal 1 RedevelopmentIn early October, MIAL proposed temporarily discontinuing 265 of CSMIA’s 770 weekly international departures from October 25 to make room at Terminal 2 for domestic flights displaced by the Terminal 1 work. Airlines quickly questioned the short notice, the capacity calculations behind the proposal, and NMIA’s readiness to accommodate more international operations.“At an airport, you require a facility for catering, for cargo warehousing. Until NMIA gets kind of fully built in the ecosystem, it’s going to be difficult for any of the airlines to shift there,” Essa Sulaiman Ahmad, Emirates senior vice-president for commercial operations in West Asia and the Indian Ocean, told the media in Delhi.The Airline Operators Committee (AOC), which represents airlines at Mumbai airport, said in a letter: “The immediate requirement is transparency on the T1 refurbishment plan, timelines, capacity assessment and operational transition.”The Ministry of Civil Aviation on October 6, the deadline for airlines to submit their proposed flight changes, asked MIAL to defer the shifting and work with airlines on a revised plan.The airport operator subsequently moved the proposed transition to the summer 2027 schedule. Its revised proposal is destination-based, with flights to 14 international destinations, including Bahrain, Dammam, Dhaka, Doha, Fujairah, Jakarta, Jeddah, Kathmandu, Kuwait City, Madinah, Muscat, Ras Al Khaimah, Riyadh and Sharjah, proposed to move to NMIA. The plan is expected to affect 12 foreign airlines.Adani Airport Holdings did not respond to Forbes India's queries. However, during the recent Aviation India event in Delhi, Arun Bansal, CEO of Adani Airport Holdings, addressed the matter, stating that redevelopment was inevitable and airlines have a "choice". “Some of the airlines have voluntarily decided to move to Navi Mumbai,” he said. “Some of the airlines might decide to suspend their operations temporarily. This is their choice.”Bansal also defended the need for the redevelopment, referring to the fire at Terminal 1 in April 2026 and the findings of independent structural consultants. Adani Airport Holdings has maintained that the transition to NMIA is temporary and does not represent a permanent shift of Mumbai airport traffic. The operator has said it will restore historical slots, along with additional slots, once the redeveloped terminal is operational.After weeks of disagreement, IndiGo and Air India Express announced their transition plans in separate statements with Adani Airport Holdings. IndiGo will progressively transfer 12 daily international departures between February and July 2027. Air India Express will start four daily domestic flights in December, followed by services to Oman and Kuwait from January 2027, subject to the necessary approvals. It will progressively move services to Jeddah, Riyadh, Dammam, Doha, Muscat and Sharjah, with the process expected to be completed by the IATA Northern Summer 2027 season. Akasa Air will move its Mumbai-Jeddah flights to NMIA from December 2026.Passenger woesNMIA has bus services connecting it with parts of Mumbai and Navi Mumbai. Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation services have announced fares of Rs 170 to Dadar East and Rs 210 to Borivali from the airport. A complimentary shuttle between NMIA and CSMIA has also been announced, with an hourly frequency.The ground reality looks different though. In April, the Indian Express reported that passengers at NMIA had struggled to find cabs, with one traveller saying a late-night journey to Virar could cost as much as Rs6,000. In June, during a cab strike, the newspaper reported that a passenger paid Rs3,200 for a prepaid taxi to Andheri East. There is a proposal to connect the two airports with a Metro, but that will take time.“Passengers could find themselves paying more [because of travel] even if airfares remain unchanged. Airport transitions often shift costs rather than reduce them,” Ashish Chhawchcharia, partner and aviation industry leader at Grant Thornton Bharat, tells Forbes India. He warns that splitting operations between the two airports could complicate connecting journeys. “Travellers need to pay closer attention to which airport they are flying from, connection windows become tighter, and self-transfer itineraries become riskier,” he adds.The airport operator has proposed cash vouchers to offset the difference in User Development Fees (UDF) between NMIA and CSMIA. The UDF is a passenger charge collected as part of the air ticket. The charge at NMIA is higher than at CSMIA, which could make tickets involving the new airport more expensive. However, the exact difference depends on the applicable passenger and flight category. The voucher amount, eligibility and redemption mechanism have not been specified.Also Read: India needs three national carriers: Adani Airports CEOWhat about the airlines?One of the incentives for airlines to shift international services to NMIA is a waiver on landing charges. On September 8, AERA revised the airport’s tariff framework to make international routes eligible for the waiver even if the same destinations were already served from the Mumbai airport. Eligible international routes receive a 100 percent waiver on landing charges in the first year, followed by a 50 percent discount in the second. Long-haul routes also qualify for a 25 percent discount in the third year.The incentives may help airlines test demand, but they will not necessarily translate into lower fares, Chhawchcharia says. Landing charges are only one component of an airline’s operating costs, alongside maintenance, personnel and other fixed expenses. Airfares are influenced more by demand, competition and capacity.He describes the waiver as a “risk-sharing mechanism” that lowers the financial barrier for airlines testing demand at a new airport. The longer-term test, he adds, is whether connectivity and passenger convenience make NMIA commercially attractive after the incentives taper off.At Aviation India, IndiGo CEO Willie Walsh said the airline saw Navi Mumbai as a long-term opportunity, given its ambition to expand its international network.“Navi Mumbai represents a big opportunity for IndiGo, given our ambition to grow our local international network,” Walsh said. He added that the airline's future would be at both Mumbai and Navi Mumbai. He also acknowledged the need to renovate Terminal 1, saying it was badly in need of work, and said IndiGo was willing to work with the airport operator on the transition.

In June, during a cab strike, the newspaper reported that a passenger paid Rs3,200 for a prepaid taxi to Andheri East.

“Passengers could find themselves paying more [because of travel] even if airfares remain unchanged.

However, the exact difference depends on the applicable passenger and flight category.

Eligible international routes receive a 100 percent waiver on landing charges in the first year, followed by a 50 percent discount in the second.

Landing charges are only one component of an airline’s operating costs, alongside maintenance, personnel and other fixed expenses.
Airfares are influenced more by demand, competition and capacity.
He describes the waiver as a “risk-sharing mechanism” that lowers the financial barrier for airlines testing demand at a new airport.
The longer-term test, he adds, is whether connectivity and passenger convenience make NMIA commercially attractive after the incentives taper off.
At Aviation India, IndiGo CEO Willie Walsh said the airline saw Navi Mumbai as a long-term opportunity, given its ambition to expand its international network.
“Navi Mumbai represents a big opportunity for IndiGo, given our ambition to grow our local international network,” Walsh said.
He added that the airline's future would be at both Mumbai and Navi Mumbai.
He also acknowledged the need to renovate Terminal 1, saying it was badly in need of work, and said IndiGo was willing to work with the airport operator on the transition.

stories.title: Cabinet approves extension of metro line from Noida Sector 51 to Greater Noida Sector 4
stories.summary: Once the corridor is open, Noida and Greater Noida city will have 71.88 km of active metro rail network; the phase aims to integrate key zones of Noida, including commercial hubs
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) approved extending the Aqua Line Metro Rail Corridor of the Noida Metro Rail Project from Noida Sector-51 to Greater Noida Sector 4 with an 8.45-km corridor and five elevated stations.
Once the corridor is open, Noida and Greater Noida city will have 71.88 km of active metro rail network.

“Extension of Aqua Line Metro Rail Corridor from Noida Sector-51 to Greater Noida Sector-04 of the Noida Metro project will introduce approximately 8.449 km of new metro lines, significantly improving public transportation in the Noida and Greater Noida city, which currently lack efficient connectivity and also it will also provide direct connectivity with high-demand corridors, including interchange at Noida Sector-61 Blue Line,” an official statement said.

The phase aims to integrate key zones of Noida, including commercial hubs such as Gaur City Mall, H&S Mall, Blue Sapphire Mall, commercial space at Greater Noida Sector-04, IKEA at Noida Sector-51, and Anthurium Mall at Noida Sector-73.
Major MNCs and IT hubs such as the Tech Mahindra office, TCL Tech office at Noida Sector-60, the Oil Industry Development Board at Noida Sector-73, and the Golden.
I office and commercial space at Greater Noida Sector-04 will be connected.

Educational institutes such as Delhi Public School at Noida Sector-122, critical healthcare facilities, most notably the Kailash Hospital and Rama Hospital at Noida Sector-70, Cloud9 Hospital at Noida Sector-51, and Rama Hospital at Noida Sector-62, and major residential societies such as Cleo County Residencies at Noida Sector-122 and Gaur City 1 and 2 at Greater Noida Sector-04 would also benefit.
